text: How did you reflect on the game the other night defensively?
Yeah.
I know you had a lot of criticism.
Did you see some progress?
Yeah, there was a little improvement, you know, with the communication and stuff like that.
Obviously, it's not up to our standard and where we want to be as a defense as a whole, but there was a little improvement.
You know, late in the game, we had some key situations where we did make some key stops when we needed to, but, you know,
ultimately, we got to tackle better.
Yeah.
How do you improve upon that?
like in season when physicality is probably less during the week?
Yeah, just the drills that we do, emphasizing the techniques on, you know, our tackling drills and things like that that we do every day.
Buck, you've been in a position before where you got hurt and you worked last season when you worked so hard to get back and you came back and you ended up missing the rest of the season.
Alex is kind of in a similar situation.
What have you seen from him the last few months and even the last couple days?
Hey, I can't speak on his injury.
You know, but I mean, I know that he's doing everything that he can to be out there on the field.
CJ Allen, obviously, in his situation, the top draft pick, low his expectations.
He had these injuries.
Have you observed just how he's handled this?
And number one and number two, you know, what kind of potential do you think is there?
We haven't seen a lot of him.
Yeah, he has a lot of potential to be a really good player in this league.
Obviously, you know, he's a young guy, but there's a lot of expectation that comes with it.
But I think he's handling it well each and every day.
You know, he's giving giving everything that he has.
I mean, he gets in here early, you know, doing all the right things.
So, you know, I mean, it's just a matter of time.
We started expecting or seeing, you know what I mean, the progress that he's made.
DeForest, when so many of these games come down to single scores to decide, obviously, you know, especially with the divisional games, obviously, usually very tight games.
Yeah.
You've talked about it, guys have reiterated needing to finish games better.
How do you apply or implement that?
Can you practice it?
Is it a mindset?
How do you figure that out?
It's definitely a mindset, a sense of urgency.
You just got to develop that killer instinct.
At the end of when you have a team where you want them, you got to finish.
And it comes down to a couple plays and it comes down to execution.
You face tough quarterbacks all the time already, but what does C .J.
Stroud offer you?
What is the difficulty providing?
Yeah,

you know, when he doesn't have certain looks and, you know, you're not really conscious of your rush lanes and things like that, that's when he's able to extend plays, you know, up the middle, gaining first downs for his team and making those, you know,
those late in the lay in the down plays.
So we've got to do a really good job with being conscious with the rush lanes.
I feel like that's almost every quarterback nowadays, you know what I mean?
More of the dual threat.
But yeah, he can't hurt us with his legs.
He's extended plays where he's holding on to the ball, and he's launching it downfield and things like that, making a play.
So we've got to do a really good job with applying pressure
on him.
And when we get back there, we've got to finish.
The green dot change to Akeem just early last week, what did you observe in the game and how that process and that change goes?
No, yeah, I mean,
like I said, I felt like the communication was definitely improved from week one.
Like I said, it's not where we want it to be, and it's not just on, you know, the green dot.
It's everybody else, you know what I mean, like executing the call, knowing where to line up, and just, you know, having your ears open for the certain checks.
So, I mean, that's the defense as a whole, you know what I mean?
But like I said, there was definitely some improvements.
How much of that do you expect to have when you have a defense that's got a lot of younger guys taking on some bigger roles?
Is that something that in week two you would still expect to have some of, or is it something that you feel like you should?
I would expect to fix it.
You know what I mean?
You're out there.
Yeah, I mean, you've got to be studying in your playbook and things like that and, you know, emphasizing the communication and being on the details.
and yeah I mean it's not expecting to have miscommunication we're expected to execute

I mean I feel like it's too early in the season we're only two we have a lot of you know we have a lot of games ahead of us and we know the type of team that we can be and we are and we just I mean it just comes down to you know the pure execution of certain things.
There have been some unflattering numbers you guys are pretty far down in the standings.
Do you have to address those like head on even though I'm sure you believe you're not the worst defense.
Not yet I mean we have I feel like we have and a lot of it comes down to tackling.
We spoke about it on Monday.
All the yards,
a lot of the yards are coming from missed tackles.
It's just routine tackles that you should be making.
That comes down to the details and your technique.
And also obviously some misalignments and little things like that which comes with the communication.
So yeah, we've been really talking about it, emphasizing it, and rubbing it.
All right.
Thanks, Brian.
All right.
Thank you.
They fly around.
They fly around to the ball.
They got game records on the defensive side of the ball.
So it's always a challenge.
You know those divisional games, it's always a challenge.
It doesn't matter what the record shows.
It doesn't matter what's going on on the other side, you know, in the building.
It's like it's going to be a four -quarter match.
And like I said, you guys have seen over the years, it does not matter what's going on.
So, obviously, we've seen them a few times, and it's going to come down to execution.
It's going to come down to execution.
And I guess that's every game, but especially this game, like I mentioned, not a whole lot, but they definitely fly around.
You know, we have to be physical this game.
These games between you guys are always heated, right?
But under the circumstances, what do you expect?
I mean, both 0 -2, both, like, kind of desperate for a win.
Like, how does that change the complexion of the game?
I just think it intensifies it and amplifies it.
Because, like you mentioned, it's always – division games, they're always intense.
But when you've got both teams that are hungry, starving, it's going to come down to who wants it more, you know, who's going to be a more physical team.
With Alec, does it change anything for you?
Like, obviously as a receiver, but whether it's how defenses attack you guys as an offense, like, does it change much for you?
Well, it definitely changes, like you mentioned, how defenses may try to attack us.
then I guess trickling down to me is, you know, how can I impact the game knowing that that's going to be even more of a point of emphasis.
They may think that they can exploit that.
So for me, it's how can I impact the game in whatever way it is, with the ball, without the ball, what can I do to ensure that whatever their game plan is, we can kind of find chinks in that armor.
When you have a big 30, 40, 50 -plus yard run, Is that something in a game where you can sense something like that coming, like you see how a defense is attacking you?

Do you feel like there's potential for that lane to open up, or is it something that kind of just happens on a given play and you're always attacking each play the same way and hoping that that opens up?

You always attack each play differently as far as like, hey, or I guess in the same way, like, hey, I'm going to go through my reads, go through my keys, but you can definitely feel like throughout the week if we know we want to have a certain plan and we know that eventually we may come to something, you know, come to something

else that, you know, I can see like, hey, they're leaning, they're leaning, or even if things are tight, a bunch of five -yard runs, six -yard runs, you can just feel when a defense just starts, you know, a little bit softer, a little bit softer, and you're like, okay, one of these I'm going to run through an arm tackle.
So you can definitely sense in some instances where, you know, something's about to open up.
There was a quote I think you gave somebody about outside zone, you know, what's the best cutback lane, and you said no cutback.
Best cut is no cut.
Best cut is no cut, yeah.
Can you explain that a little bit?
I mean, as a runner, especially in the backfield,
what is the number one thing that usually gets you tackled?
It's stopping your feet, breaking your feet, getting off your track, making a move, you know, pursuit angle.
So if you can not cut at all, that's the best cut because you keep your speed, you keep your power, you keep your momentum, and you're just off and running.
How, like your touchdown runs last week, How have you developed the patience?
Because like a 24 -yard, you waited a long time before you turned it up.
How have you developed the patience to know that you don't have to cut it up?
Well, really, I understand.
It's about trust, too, as well.
That's a big thing.
I know a lot of younger backs, when you come from high school going into college, usually, for the most part, you're bigger, faster, stronger than everybody.
So you're out running a defender on the edge.
You're doing a bunch of crazy stuff.

and you know once you get to college and you really learn like okay there's a there's a way this play is supposed to develop there's a scheme to it it's a thought process behind it and then obviously getting to this level everything is critical and obviously these are the best guys in the world so you got to have the utmost space faith

and trust in those guys up front like hey I'm following my guys like I know they're going to get it done so I don't need to break my feet I don't need to think twice because we've repped this weekend and week out or throughout the entire week, whatever the scheme is.
So it's about trust, but it's also understanding that these are the best guys.
So you're not just going to be able to outrun everybody and go rogue on any given scheme.
So on that longer touchdown, I think you're going to the right, there's a defense back over there on the other side.
And are you watching him or are you just waiting on your guys?
What are you thinking when you're navigating that?
You got to feel 1c2.
You feel 1c2, so I'm feeling my guys up front, but I'm watching the second level defender.
and I'm really reading off him.
I'm trying to deliver him to my blockers.
That's what your job is as a back.
You want to help your guys.
They can't see where you're at, so it's your job to help navigate and guide them to the guy that you want.
JT, you talked about trust.
When was that point that you found that level of trust with the group that you have now, predominantly the same group of guys that you had in the last two years?
Like you said, we really had the same group of guys, But I just think when I first got here and going through that first year and understand there were a couple plays where, you know,

doing some things that I might have done in college, you know, going rogue a little bit, I like to call it, and you see the yards that you leave out there and then you see the work that your guys up front put in
and you see when they turn around and they don't see you.
They're like, well, what's going on?
So that's the feeling that you don't want.

So I think after going through that first year and understanding, like, I don't want to let my guys down, but then also like, hey, we left a lot of yards out there, so maybe that could have impacted the game in a different way.
You talk about attention to detail and execution.
Houston's won the last five all one -score games.
I bet you can go in every game and say, just play that.
But is it that's – I mean, can't you?
Yeah, and that's what it comes down to ultimately with these type of games because everyone's so locked in, they're so honed in because you know like how important these division games are.
And then on those few plays, whichever game it is, it's like that was probably the difference maker.
These couple of plays right here were the difference maker.
So what can you do to either be better prepared, execute better, out will?
It's like it's going to come down to just a few things.
And I think everyone has to have that mentality.
I think they do.
For both teams, it's like what can I do to make sure that those one or two plays go our way?
Same thing with Kansas City last week.
Definitely.
I'll play here and play there, and then it's totally different.
Definitely.
